summary: Preinstall dropper downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 728KB payload
details: The package publishes under the @servicetitan npm scope but its declared main (dist/index.js) is a trivial re-export of ionicons icons with a stub ExampleComponent, empty README, and empty author — a metadata shape consistent with dependency-confusion impersonation of a private @servicetitan package. Its package.json declares a preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a bundled math_init.js file. math_init.js is a 728KB single-line Bun-compiled script whose contents are obfuscated with a rotated string-array cipher (integer/charset table + array-shift rotator, `@bun @bun-cjs` header) and are unrelated to the package's advertised purpose of React components for mobile webviews. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator-style hex identifiers and per-function string maps, hiding the download-and-execute logic from reviewers. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern (fetch an alien runtime, then execute an opaque bundled payload under it) evades Node-based static scanners; the payload runs with the installer's privileges at `npm install` time inside developer and CI environments.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
